piCurve 0.4.5
  • Reference

Estimate clear-sky sea-surface spectral irradiance

Source: R/ss_irad.R
sea_surface_irradiance_piCurve.Rd

Estimates downwelling clear-sky spectral irradiance at the sea surface using a Gregg and Carder (1990) parameterization for cloudless maritime atmospheres.

sea_surface_irradiance_piCurve(
  zenith_angle,
  database_info,
  sample_date,
  H_oz = 266,
  data_climato_solar = NULL
)

Source

Gregg, W. W., & Carder, K. L. (1990). A simple spectral solar irradiance model for cloudless maritime atmospheres. Journal of Geophysical Research.

Arguments

zenith_angle

Numeric scalar. Solar zenith angle in degrees (0 <= zenith_angle < 90). Users may estimate solar zenith angle using solar_zenith_angle_piCurve().

database_info

Data frame containing wavelength-specific optical inputs. Must contain the following columns:

lambda

Wavelength in vacuo (nm).

H_o

Spectral extraterrestrial solar irradiance (W m\(^{-2}\) nm\(^{-1}\)).

a_oz

Ozone absorption coefficient (cm\(^{-1}\)).

a_w

Water vapor absorption coefficient (cm\(^{-1}\)).

a_o

Oxygen absorption coefficient (cm\(^{-1}\)).

sample_date

A date coercible to Date. Used to compute orbital correction of extraterrestrial irradiance.

H_oz

Numeric scalar. Total column ozone depth in Dobson Units (DU). Default is 266. If not supplied, users may estimate ozone depth using ozone_depth_piCurve().

data_climato_solar

Optional list or one-row data frame of atmospheric inputs (e.g., pressure, water vapor, aerosol properties). If NULL, default climatological values are used.

Value

A data frame with columns:

wavelength

Wavelength (nm).

irradiance

Estimated downwelling spectral irradiance at the sea surface (W m\(^{-2}\) nm\(^{-1}\)).

Details

This function implements a spectral clear-sky irradiance model following Gregg and Carder (1990), combining atmospheric transmittance due to:

  • Rayleigh scattering

  • Oxygen absorption

  • Water vapor absorption

  • Ozone absorption

  • Aerosol scattering and absorption

  • Air–sea surface reflectance

Spectral irradiance is computed as a function of wavelength and solar zenith angle, with extraterrestrial irradiance corrected for Earth–Sun distance based on day of year.

NOTE: Unit consistency is required:

  • Wavelength (lambda) must be provided in nanometers (nm).

  • Extraterrestrial irradiance (H_o) must be in W m\(^{-2}\) nm\(^{-1}\).

  • Absorption coefficients (a_oz, a_w, a_o) must be in cm\(^{-1}\).

  • Ozone depth (H_oz) must be in Dobson Units (DU).

The function returns spectral irradiance. Photosynthetically available radiation (PAR) can be obtained by integrating output irradiance over 400–700 nm.

The dataset GreggCarder1990 provides a standard set of coefficients consistent with this formulation.

Examples

# Example with synthetic coefficients
db <- data.frame(
  lambda = c(400, 500, 600),
  a_o = c(0.01, 0.02, 0.01),
  a_w = c(0.00, 0.01, 0.02),
  a_oz = c(0.03, 0.02, 0.01),
  H_o = c(1.8, 1.9, 1.7)
)

sea_surface_irradiance_piCurve(
  zenith_angle = 30,
  database_info = db,
  sample_date = "2024-07-24"
)
#>   wavelength irradiance
#> 1        400   1.437485
#> 2        500   1.505204
#> 3        600   1.356519

# Example using Gregg & Carder (1990) dataset
sea_surface_irradiance_piCurve(
  zenith_angle = 30,
  database_info = GreggCarder1990,
  sample_date = "2024-07-24"
)

# Example based on coordinators & time (unknown zenith angle)
DATE <- as.Date("2024-03-20")
zn <- solar_zenith_angle_piCurve(DATE, time = "12:00:00", latitude = 0, longitude = 0)

SSirad <- sea_surface_irradiance_piCurve(zenith_angle = zn, database_info = GreggCarder1990, sample_date = DATE)
head(SSirad, 3)
#>   wavelength irradiance
#> 1        350  0.8363407
#> 2        351  0.8287454
#> 3        352  0.8259550
